executiveSummary: GM0275 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service numerical contract and has a coherent official 2025 base: Rheden in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Midden, 43,782 residents, density 535, 27.2% aged 65-plus, 9,105 one-person households, 23 neighbourhoods in three districts, seven BAG woonplaatsen and eight BRT settlement labels. Rounded neighbourhood populations sum to 43,770, only twelve below the separately published municipality control (-0.027%). Operational release is nevertheless correction-required. Rheden spans the IJssel floodplain, settlements and infrastructure below the steep Veluwezoom, with brook, pluvial, sewer, groundwater and high-water pathways, extensive forest and recreation, and divided water governance. The river preset instead holds an internal generic flood-stress amplitude of 2.516093 and severity 0.792919 from T+24 through T+72 without a selected IJssel boundary, defence, floodplain, brook, sewer, groundwater or asset state. Eight unrelated active presets reuse exactly the same 23-neighbourhood severity order. A controlled fire placed in the forest neighbourhood at De Steeg ranks that source only tenth while resident-only allocation cannot represent visitors in zero- or near-zero-resident forest rows. Three logical road links omit/reduce important A348/N348/N786, Arnhem, rail and ferry access semantics; public registers and webpage status do not establish live passage, topology, capacity, backup or restoration. De Steeg water forecasts end at T+24, so exact T+48/T+72 effects, clearance and service recovery lack accountable evidence and actions. Unknown, NoData, static-register and planning values must never become zero hazard, safe, open, available or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Gebiedsindelingen 2025, Kerncijfers wijken en buurten, BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlement context
supports: GM0275 Rheden identity, Gelderland and Gelderland-Midden assignment, generalized boundary and centre 6.0446128, 52.0419118
43,782 residents, density 535, 27.2% aged 65-plus and 9,105 one-person households in the municipality control
Twenty-three neighbourhood rows in three districts; rounded populations total 43,770, households 21,465 and age-65-plus counts 11,925
Seven BAG woonplaatsen are De Steeg, Dieren, Ellecom, Laag-Soeren, Rheden, Spankeren and Velp; BRT adds Elleburg as a gehucht to seven woonkern labels
CBS and BRT reuse is CC BY 4.0 and BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0; these are annual administrative, statistical and register facts rather than incident-time occupancy or hazard calibration

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Ruimte voor klimaat: Lokale Adaptatie Strategie
supports: Rheden's current adaptation policy treats heat and health, drought, pluvial nuisance, flood safety and nature fire as distinct climate themes
The strategy calls for robust green-blue structures, restoration of old brooks and development directed by water and soil
The page establishes local hazard eligibility and policy direction, not a selected incident, calibrated footprint, present operating state, response capacity or T+72 outcome
A standard webpage reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Gebiedsproces Zuidflank Veluwezoom
evidenceSources.edition: municipality page updated 2026-07-30; process in pre-exploration
supports: The Doorwerth-to-Dieren southern Veluwe flank is geomorphologically complex and faces connected water, ecology, cultural-landscape, urban and recreation pressures

The process is building a fact base for a robust water and soil system with Rheden, neighbouring municipalities, Province Gelderland, Waterschap Rijn en IJssel, Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe, Vitens and land managers
Joint participation confirms divided catchment and service governance but does not identify live topology, capacity, asset state or authority-selected incident hydraulics
This is planning-lifecycle evidence, not an implemented measure or operating commitment; a standard reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Gladheid, winter closure and high-water access guidance
supports: Vehicle roads over the Posbank and Rozendaalse Veld can close during snow or freezing; salt is not used in protected nature and the terrain can make snow clearing impossible
The municipality names three high-water closure areas: Havikerwaard, the floodplains from Velp to Rheden and the area at the IJssel bridge between Velp and Westervoort
These are credible mechanism and access-control rules, not proof that any road is currently closed or open, nor a route-capacity or reopening forecast
A standard webpage reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Rural pump-pit, IBA and heavy-rain sewer guidance
supports: Some rural properties discharge through a municipal pump pit with an electrical cabinet and warning light, while others use an individual wastewater-treatment system
Heavy rain can overload the sewer and cause backflow through toilets or sinks
The guidance establishes a power-drainage and pluvial-sewer dependency but gives no complete catchment, live pump state, backup, capacity, blockage or restoration commitment
A standard webpage reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Current regional risk profile and preparedness context
supports: VGGM currently ranks flooding and epidemics highest in Gelderland-Midden, followed by nature fire, cyber and utility disruption among the leading risks

Regional public guidance promotes warning reception, emergency supplies and 72-hour self-reliance; municipalities were preparing support points in 2026, but the public material names no operational Rheden point, staffing, stock or capacity
Risk ranking and preparedness plans support eligibility and governance, not a GM0275 event amplitude, live resource state, probability, local outcome or recovery promise
A standard webpage reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Bezoekerscentrum and Masterplan Veluwezoom visitor-distribution context
supports: Nationaal Park Veluwezoom comprises more than 5,200 hectares of forest, heath and sand and is described by its manager as heavily visited
The current masterplan distributes visitor pressure and uses summer, weekend and holiday vehicle-access measures, with Rheden station linked to the visitor centre

The source establishes combustible-land-cover, recreation and time-varying access/exposure eligibility, not visitor counts, live occupancy, ignition, fuel moisture, perimeter, plume or suppression capacity
A standard webpage reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / RIVM / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / PDOK-KVK
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Deployed public water, transport, care, utility, antenna, education and government-service context
supports: HWH containment assigns 116 realized water records inside GM0275: 17 sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps, one sluice and 95 weirs; managers include Waterschap Rijn en IJssel and Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe, and most public capacities are null
De Steeg Waterinfo observed 494 cm NAP at 2026-09-02T17:30Z; deployed forecasts at T+1, T+6, T+12 and T+24 are 496, 496, 497 and 497 cm NAP, with no GM0275 T+48/T+72 forecast features

The generated transport context contains only three logical N785/N317/N348 cross-boundary edges, three ProRail stations and 117 GTFS stop areas; logical capacities are non-additive planning proxies rather than physical throughput

No RIVM acute-care site is inside GM0275; the centre-to-Rijnstate Arnhem reference distance is about 10.32 km, while one 6994CN NBNL Liander sample, 59 antenna records, 37 education locations and four government-service points are static or planning context

HWH is CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness; Waterinfo is generally CC0 and not mission-critical; register presence, point observations, schedules and planning samples do not establish connected topology, municipality-wide impact, live continuity, capacity, backup, accessibility or recovery

evidenceSources.title: E09 — Public ferry operating-status webpage
evidenceSources.edition: human-readable current page accessed 2026-09-03; no reliable issue or expiry time published
supports: The operator page displayed that the Dieren-Olburgen ferry was out of service because of low water when inspected
The ferry is absent from the deployed GTFS ferry-route context, demonstrating that a schedule catalogue can omit a locally relevant crossing
A human-readable webpage without reliable issue and expiry time cannot be projected as a T+0 to T+72 operating state or generalized to other crossings
A standard webpage reuse licence was not stated

identity.summary: Official 2025 identity, regional assignment, centre and generalized boundary agree.
notes: Manifest, generated context and official features identify GM0275 as Rheden in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Midden.
The generated centre 6.0446128, 52.0419118 lies inside the official generalized 2025 boundary.
The boundary is administrative context, not a hydraulic, fire, smoke, infrastructure, service or response footprint.

geography.summary: The administrative footprint is coherent but cannot encode the IJssel-floodplain and Veluwezoom water, fire and access mechanisms.
notes: Rheden joins steep and forested Veluwezoom terrain, brook and urban-flank flow paths, settlements, the Apeldoorn Canal and low IJssel floodplain areas with materially different mechanisms.
Generalized boundaries and centre points do not encode elevation, flow paths, floodplain/defence side, groundwater, sewers, water assets, fuel, buildings or route intersections.
The Rivierklimaatpark IJsselpoort structure vision and current plan development support long-term room-for-river context only; they are not live hydraulic or defence state.

demography.summary: The official municipality control and rounded neighbourhood totals are internally plausible.
notes: The municipality control is 43,782 residents; neighbourhood rows total 43,770, a difference of -12 or -0.027% consistent with source rounding.
Municipality statistics report density 535, 27.2% aged 65-plus and 9,105 one-person households; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 21,465 households and 11,925 people aged 65-plus.
Registered residents are not incident-time people present and exclude visitors, workers, pupils, patients, ferry/rail passengers and recreation populations.

regionalDetail.summary: Twenty-three neighbourhoods provide useful demographic context but contain explicit nulls and no physical hazard calibration.
notes: All 23 rows contain population and age bands; home/tenure fields cover 18, doctor and supermarket distance 19, household size 21 and cars per household 14.
District-heating percentage and public charging points are unavailable in all 23 rows; null and catalogue no-match remain Unknown or NoData rather than zero.
Two official forest rows, BU02750010 at Ellecom and BU02750011 at Dieren, have zero registered residents but retain non-residential buildings; this is not zero people present or zero service demand.

settlements.summary: BAG and BRT place membership is coherent when their distinct semantics are preserved.
notes: Seven BAG woonplaatsen have centres inside the generalized boundary; BRT supplies seven woonkernen plus Elleburg as one gehucht.
BAG address registration and BRT cartographic labels are complementary and must not be treated as duplicate populations.
Settlements do not provide incident-time occupancy, evacuation zones, service catchments or hazard cells.

transport.summary: Static road, rail, transit and ferry identity is incomplete for event-valid access and external-care routing.
notes: The generated graph has only N785 to Rozendaal, N317 to Doesburg and N348 to Brummen; it does not express the full A348/N348/N786 system, direct Arnhem dependency, rail corridors or ferry crossings.
Velp, Rheden and Dieren stations and 117 stop areas are static; the Dieren-Olburgen page status lacked reliable issue/expiry time and is not a T+72 state.

Known high-water zones and winter Posbank closure rules matter to direction-aware routes, but no selected hazard intersection, current restriction, emergency throughput or reopening milestone is consumed.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong municipal, water-system, nature-manager and regional preparedness context exists, but decision-ready incident state and capacity do not.
notes: Rheden and VGGM establish material flood, pluvial, groundwater, heat, drought, nature-fire, cyber and utility concerns plus 72-hour self-reliance guidance.

No public source identifies an activated Rheden support point, its role, staffing, accessibility, supplies or capacity; general NL-Alert, shelter, evacuation and neighbour-support guidance is not an incident action ledger.
No selected incident supplies an accountable owner, issue/valid time, geometry or target, measured state, probability, uncertainty, response resources or recovery verification.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six checkpoints across all eight services.
notes: Focused audit:model covers T+0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours for severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound.
The app scenario factory clones the canonical sim-core presets; direct full-network reproductions used the deployed municipality, regional and transport bundles.
Coverage is not calibration: outputs are deterministic exercise indices, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, allocation, burden and layer-invariance contracts pass.
notes: Focused tests passed two of two cases; outputs are finite and non-negative, availability remains in [0,1], zero-event behavior is exact and cumulative person-hours are monotone.
All service allocations use 23 neighbourhoods and reconcile to the 43,782 control; service-layer selection does not mutate hazard state.
Arithmetic correctness does not validate local forcing, physical allocation, topology, actions or recovery.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic IJssel allocation, shared cross-hazard ranks and a controlled forest-source test fail local physical plausibility.
notes: River T+24, T+48 and T+72 each report internal flood stress 2.516093 and severity 0.792919 without a selected IJssel boundary, defence/floodplain, brook, groundwater, sewer or asset surface.
At T+24 eight active presets reuse exactly the same 23-neighbourhood order, led by Laag-Soeren, Dieren-West and Velp-Zuid-below-rail, irrespective of mechanism.

A controlled T+24 wildfire centred in BU02750106 Verspreide huizen bosgebied De Steeg produces severity 0.728286 and direct fire 0.777917, yet ranks its source only tenth of 23; its registered population is five and estimated affected two.
No terrain, drainage, defence, current vegetation/fuel, ignition/perimeter/spread, plume, building, vulnerable-person or operator target surface drives those allocations.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service trajectories are synthetic and do not consume Rheden's water, power, access, care and telecom dependencies.
notes: HWH exposes 116 contained assets divided between Rijn en IJssel, Vallei en Veluwe and incomplete manager fields, but no approved connected topology, compatible capacity, live state, power/backup or restoration is consumed.

The municipal pump-pit guidance establishes electricity dependence for rural drainage, while the one NBNL sample is planning context and RDI antennas expose no live power, backhaul or coverage continuity.
No acute-care site is inside GM0275; straight-line Rijnstate proximity does not prove an accessible route, ambulance/referral state, receiving capacity, staffing, occupancy or generator endurance.
Power, drinking water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply nevertheless receive exact availability, demand, reserve, status and recovery values.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic ledgers reconcile but cannot explain locally supported hazard-to-service-to-people causality.
notes: River reports exactly 26,320 affected at both T+48 and T+72; compound T+72 reports flood stress 0.480339, cyber stress 0.048027, severity 0.414258 and 25,074 affected.

At T+72 severe storm, pluvial and canonical wildfire have zero forcing and zero affected plus an operational aggregate label despite accumulated burdens of about 305,733, 447,305 and 271,007 person-hours.

Synthetic severity and one resident-weighted allocation seed drive demand and availability without showing which IJssel/flank/fire/cyber cell, asset, route, cohort or accountable action caused each change.
The UI must distinguish Assumption, Official register, Observation, Forecast, Planning, Unknown and NoData and suppress unsupported exact decimals and safe/open/recovered implications.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 persistence, exact clearance and recovery labels lack owner-verified local milestones.
notes: River remains at stress 2.516093, severity 0.792919 and 26,320 affected from T+48 through T+72 while cumulative burden rises to about 1,649,003 person-hours.
Pluvial and canonical wildfire become exact zero forcing/affected and operational at T+72, whereas compound remains critical with about 1,558,771 cumulative person-hours.
De Steeg public forecasts stop at T+24; lack of T+48/T+72 features is NoData and neither confirms persistence nor an all-clear.
No accountable T+0-to-T+72 warning, evacuation/shelter, water-control, fire, access, lifeline, care, support-point, re-entry or verification ledger supports these transitions.

findings.summary: The official identity, demographic control and distinct place semantics reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM0275 Rheden, Gelderland, Gelderland-Midden, the official centre and generalized boundary agree. Twenty-three rounded neighbourhood populations total 43,770 versus the 43,782 municipality control, a -0.027% difference; seven BAG places and eight BRT labels have distinct valid semantics.
findings.action: Retain edition, rounding, suppression and register semantics; never turn controls, place labels or official-zero resident cells into incident-time occupancy.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical and coverage contract passes.
findings.evidence: Ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services execute deterministically with finite bounded values, reconciliation, causal arithmetic, monotone cumulative burden and layer invariance; the focused test ran two cases and both passed.
findings.action: Keep GM0275 in regression and add local IJssel/flank/fire/dynamic-exposure/access/NoData and recovery-action assertions.

findings.summary: A real IJssel pathway is represented by unsupported generic forcing, footprint and precision.
findings.evidence: At T+24, T+48 and T+72 the model reports internal flood stress 2.516093 and severity 0.792919; T+48/T+72 both report 26,320 affected. Rheden evidence identifies high-water access areas and long-term room-for-river work, but no selected IJssel/De Steeg boundary condition, defence and floodplain state, breach/overtopping, depth/velocity/arrival/recession surface, uncertainty or intervention supports the value.
findings.action: Keep IJssel high water eligible but withhold local consequence and recovery until an authority-selected event binds named hydraulic and defence evidence; unresolved cells remain Unknown and the legacy scalar must not be shown as surveyed metres.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one local severity order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber, canonical wildfire and compound all rank Laag-Soeren, Dieren-West, Velp-Zuid below rail and Velp-Noord first in the same order. The allocation consumes neither IJssel/flank hydrology, fire fuel/spread, weather exposure nor cyber targets.
findings.action: Replace the shared rank with mechanism-specific physical or target surfaces and reject complete cross-hazard order reuse; unsupported neighbourhood cells remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Precise pluvial stress and clearance omit the Veluwezoom-to-IJssel water chain.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports internal flood stress 0.465593, severity 0.336261 and 7,559 affected, then exact zero forcing/affected and operational status at T+72. Municipal evidence distinguishes steep geomorphology, brooks, water/soil direction, sewer overload, groundwater and high-water receiving conditions, but no selected rain, DEM/flow path, initial groundwater, sewer, pump/weir/sluice or receiving-water state drives the values.
findings.action: Bind authoritative rain to terrain, brook/surface-water, groundwater/kwel, sewer, pump and receiving-IJssel evidence with issue/valid time, resolution, uncertainty, coverage and explicit NoData.

findings.summary: Wildfire forcing and resident allocation fail a fire placed in Rheden's own forest.
findings.evidence: The canonical T+24 preset emits zero direct fire but smoke 0.486593, drought 0.672768, severity 0.178051 and 1,843 affected without local ignition evidence. In a controlled fire centred in BU02750106 forest De Steeg, direct fire is 0.777917 and municipal severity 0.728286, yet the source ranks tenth of 23 and assigns only two affected from five registered residents. Two other forest rows have official zero residents despite non-residential buildings and manager evidence of heavy, time-varying recreation.
findings.action: Use current eligible vegetation, ignition/perimeter/spread, wind/plume and response-access evidence; allocate privacy-safe time-banded visitors and other people present separately from registered residents and preserve unknown occupancy.

findings.summary: Resident-only counts cannot represent Rheden's recreation, school, work, care and transport populations.
findings.evidence: Every affected total is reconciled only to 43,782 registered residents. Veluwezoom is heavily visited, three stations and 117 stop areas are present, and 37 education locations plus workplaces, care users and ferry/rail passengers provide eligibility, but no time-varying occupancy, evacuation behavior or uncertainty is consumed.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe, time-banded people-present cohorts with authoritative provenance and uncertainty; show resident-equivalents separately from visitors, pupils, workers, patients and passengers.

findings.summary: Water-asset containment and planning partnerships do not establish connected drinking-water and drainage operation.
findings.evidence: HWH contains 116 records split across Rijn en IJssel, Vallei en Veluwe, null and generic manager values; capacities are absent for the three surface-water pumps, the sluice and 95 weirs. Zuidflank planning involves both water boards and Vitens, and rural pump pits depend on electricity. None provides a complete catchment/topology, compatible throughput, present setting, power/backup, drinking-water continuity or restoration state.
findings.action: Represent approved non-sensitive catchment and service compartments independently from asset-point containment, with authority, direction, compatible capacity, current state, dependency, uncertainty, issue/valid time and NoData.

findings.summary: The three-link graph omits or reduces critical road, rail, ferry, high-water and forest-access dependencies.
findings.evidence: Only N785, N317 and N348 logical cross-boundary edges are generated, with nominal proxy capacity 150 each. The A348/N348/N786 system, Arnhem access, three rail stations, 117 stop areas and ferry crossings are not an event-valid multimodal graph. Rheden names high-water and winter closure areas, while the Dieren-Olburgen status page had no reliable issue/expiry time.
findings.action: Build direction-aware topology from monthly NWB and operator data, intersect selected hazards and restrictions, and validate paths to settlements, forest, water controls, support points and care; never infer open, throughput or reopening from geometry, schedules or stale webpages.

findings.summary: External acute care and static power, gas and telecom registers do not justify exact continuity or recovery.
findings.evidence: No RIVM acute-care questionnaire site is inside GM0275; Rijnstate Arnhem is about 10.32 km from the municipal centre only as a straight-line reference. One NBNL postcode sample describes Liander large-user planning, and 59 antenna records are static. These do not establish routes/referral, staffing, occupancy, receiving capacity, power/gas topology, load, outage, switching, backup, telecom coverage/backhaul or restoration.
findings.action: Use GHOR/operator-approved safe aggregate incident and restoration bands with provenance and explicit Unknown; keep facility registration, provider/planning samples and antenna presence separate from operational state.

findings.summary: Point observations, short forecasts and empty catalogues are not municipality-wide live state or a T+72 all-clear.
findings.evidence: De Steeg observed 494 cm NAP at 2026-09-02T17:30Z and forecasts reach only T+24. No GM0275 Waterinfo T+48/T+72 features, local KNMI station, air station, current NDW situation or recent local seismic catalogue match was available; a provincial no-warning flag has only its own horizon. Empty/no-match is NoData, not zero water, weather, smoke, closure or shaking, and the ferry webpage state has no reliable validity window.
findings.action: Enforce publisher, issue/valid time, location/geometry, units/datum, uncertainty, coverage, licence and freshness; render Observation, Forecast, Register, Planning, Unknown and NoData distinctly and never forward-fill beyond validity.

findings.summary: Coastal, wind, heat/drought, winter, cyber and earthquake results are synthetic exercise assumptions.
findings.evidence: The inland coastal preset has zero direct flood stress but retains small wind effects; this does not test IJssel, pluvial or groundwater safety. Heat T+72 retains drought 0.478267 but zero affected, winter clears by T+72, cyber retains stress 0.042092 with zero affected, and the remote Groningen earthquake has no selected local event. None is bound to local weather, vulnerability, road, target or shaking evidence.
findings.action: Label each as an exercise assumption, separate direct from indirect effects and require authoritative source/target, issue/valid time, units, uncertainty, coverage, licence and NoData for operational use.

findings.summary: First-72-hour plateaus, clearance and operational labels lack accountable actions and verified milestones.
findings.evidence: River is unchanged from T+48 to T+72 at stress 2.516093, severity 0.792919 and 26,320 affected while burden rises to about 1,649,003 person-hours. Compound remains critical with 25,074 affected and about 1,558,771 person-hours, while storm, pluvial and wildfire become exact-zero/operational. De Steeg forecasting stops at T+24 and no owner-trigger-decision-resource-execution-verification record explains warning, evacuation, water control, access, lifelines, care, support, all-clear or re-entry.
findings.action: Replace exact T+72 labels with uncertainty bands and an accountable action/milestone ledger; state remains Unknown until the responsible authority or operator verifies the transition.

corrections.summary: Replace generic GM0275 river and pluvial stress with authority-selected IJssel, floodplain, flank, brook, groundwater and sewer event contracts.
corrections.validation: Require a named authority-selected event with IJssel/De Steeg boundary condition and datum, defence/floodplain side, connected depth/velocity/arrival/recession surface, flank/brook/groundwater/kwel/sewer/pump state, issue/valid time, uncertainty, resolution, coverage, NoData and licence. Waterinfo points validate only their own time and location; T+24 forecast termination is NoData. Reject unsupported 2.516093 persistence while retaining real high-water eligibility.

corrections.summary: Replace shared GM0275 spatial seeding with mechanism-aware geometry and source-aware fire/dynamic exposure.
corrections.validation: Use hydraulic/rain-flow cells for water, heat/vulnerability surfaces, eligible current vegetation plus ignition/perimeter/spread/plume for fire/smoke, wind exposure and asset targets for cyber. A controlled ignition in BU02750106 must not rank its source tenth solely through a common seed. Zero-resident forest cells must preserve Unknown people-present and unrelated hazards may not reuse the full severity order.

corrections.summary: Integrate Rheden's divided water chain and safe aggregate power, drinking-water, drainage, gas and telecom dependencies.
corrections.validation: Reconcile municipality, both water boards, HWH, Vitens and utility evidence into approved non-sensitive compartments. Preserve catchment and service relations independently from point containment and bind water direction, compatible capacity, current settings, electricity/backhaul/backup, uncertainty and NoData. HWH partial registers and NBNL/RDI planning/register samples cannot generate live continuity or recovery.

corrections.summary: Add event-valid A348/N348/N786, Arnhem, rail/ferry, forest/high-water and external-care access with time-banded people present.
corrections.validation: Use NWB monthly CC0 topology plus timestamped authority/operator road, rail, transit and ferry state. Intersect selected hazards with direction-aware access to settlements, forest, water controls, named support points and selected acute-care destinations; record issue/valid time, accessibility and Unknown capacity. Show registered residents separately from privacy-safe time-banded visitors, pupils, workers, patients and passengers.

corrections.summary: Replace unsupported exactness and GM0275 first-72-hour recovery labels with provenance, NoData and accountable milestones.
corrections.validation: For warnings, evacuation/shelter, IJssel/flank controls, fire response/all-clear, roads/rail/ferries, utilities, external care, vulnerable-person/visitor support, support points and re-entry, store owner, trigger, request, decision, resources, dependencies, execution, verification, issue/valid time, uncertainty and rollback. UI/tests must distinguish Assumption, Official register, Observation, Forecast, Planning, Unknown and NoData and reject exact clearance, safe/open/operational/recovered labels without verified milestones.

residualLimitations: This audit assesses a deterministic exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic/fire assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee, clinical referral or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 neighbourhood values are rounded or suppressed; the -12 population reconciliation is not evidence of missing or extra incident-time people.
Registered residents exclude visitors, workers, pupils, patients, station/ferry passengers and people in forest/recreation areas; no complete time-varying occupancy series is consumed.
Generalized boundaries and centre points are unsuitable for terrain, brook, groundwater, sewer, floodplain/defence, vegetation, building, smoke or route-intersection calculations.
Municipal climate, Zuidflank and Rivierklimaatpark material documents hazard eligibility and planning lifecycle, not a selected event, implemented measure, live hydraulic state or outcome.
Municipal high-water and winter guidance names conditional closure areas but is not current event state, direction-aware detour, throughput or reopening evidence.
Groundwater and sewer guidance supports distinct pathways but does not provide initial state, connected network, live pump/backup, capacity or restoration.
The regional risk profile and 72-hour self-reliance material do not provide municipality-specific forcing, probability, action, resource state or recovery.
Veluwezoom forest and visitor-manager context establishes fire and dynamic-exposure eligibility only; current fuel, ignition, perimeter, plume, occupancy, access and suppression remain Unknown.
HWH's 116 contained records have contributor-dependent completeness, mixed manager values and mostly null capacity; presence is not connectivity, compatible throughput, live operation or restoration.
A De Steeg point observation and forecasts ending T+24 cannot validate municipality-wide water state, connected depth or T+48/T+72 impact and recovery.
NWB, GTFS and ProRail context does not establish live direction, passability, accessibility, emergency throughput, station/rail operation or destination access.
The Dieren-Olburgen operator page lacked reliable issue and expiry time, so its inspected low-water outage cannot be projected over the model horizon or applied to other ferries.
No RIVM acute-care location lies inside GM0275; external registration and centre distance do not establish referral, route, occupancy, staffing, diversion, backup endurance or acceptance.

One NBNL postcode sample and RDI, DUO and government-service records are planning/register context, not complete topology, current load, incident, backhaul, occupancy, support role, backup or restoration.
No selected local weather, heat, fire, flood, cyber, utility, transport, care or seismic incident is bound by publisher, issue/valid time, geometry/target, units, uncertainty, coverage and licence.
Exact synthetic availability can reconcile numerically without validating physical causality, capacity, response decisions or recovery.
Recovery beyond T+72, warning lead, mutual aid, shelter/support capacity, public health, animals, prolonged displacement and long-term re-entry remain outside locally validated scope.
